items.title: As Destiny 2 is laid to rest, Warframe is experiencing 'massive growth,' studio boss says
items.summary: Digital Extremes president Sheldon Carter says the studio was worried that Warframe had peaked, but these days it
items.content:
Digital Extremes president Sheldon Carter says the studio was worried that Warframe had peaked, but these days it's doing better than ever.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter With Destiny 2 now fully embalmed , I find myself wondering—as do a great many others— 'how did this happen?' A new Game Business interview with Sheldon Carter, president of Warframe developer Digital Extremes, has me pondering that question even harder: It turns out that while Destiny 2 was floundering, its foremost rival was enjoying "a few years of straight massive growth."

Sheldon said that the original Destiny "really hit us" when it launched in 2014, well over a year after Warframe's 2013 release, and his initial instinct was to "aggressively" compete with Bungie. But that changed over the years, and like others at Digital Extremes, Carter doesn't see the end of Destiny 2 development as a welcome development.

"Over time, what happens is developers from their team come on to your team. New people who you started, they learned what looter shooters are and how that works because they put thousands of hours into Destiny," Carter said. "And so, at our studio, it was kind of a bit of mourning when they released that news. The mood in our studio was pretty dour because of all the connections that you end up having."

But while Destiny 2's player numbers were in significant decline before Sony pulled the plug, Warframe has apparently been headed in the opposite direction. Carter said that "four or five years ago," Digital Extremes began to worry that Warframe had peaked, and it was time to start thinking about what's next. That kicked off development of Soulframe , the studio's second project—but at the same time it also brought about some changes on how the studio handlined Warframe.

"We changed our focus on how we were developing the game, how we were promoting the game," Carter said. "And now we've had a few years of straight, just massive growth ... Now we're in this happy position where Warframe's really thriving, and that gives us the ability to give Soulframe a ton of rope [and] time to really try stuff out and connect."

'There is no world where it makes sense,' Warframe creative director says of Destiny 2's demise: 'It's unthinkable' Warframe dev says 'no one is celebrating' Destiny 2 winding down: 'A game is healthy when you have competitors' Warframe creative director says Destiny 2's end is tragic, because even with hard work 'the business side of this industry always gets the last remark' Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’ - YouTube Watch On That's something else Digital Extremes seems to be doing differently: Where Bungie poured valuable time and resources into numerous "incubation projects" that went nowhere , Digital Extremes is moving very deliberately on a single project—Soulframe—which, four years after it was announced , is still in pre-release and not available on Steam.

"I think one of the things you learn as you do a second game that you're trying for the same scope as something like Warframe is that expertise doesn't necessarily mean you don't make the same mistakes as you did before," Carter said. "It just means you can recover from them a little bit faster.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"So that's been the journey of Soulframe—relearning a few of the things that we forgot after so many years, but at the same time using that core [audience], which is just establishing communication, building trust with the audience, and taking our time to get it to a point where we feel like there's enough content, enough story, enough gameplay that when we release it to a wider audience, um it's going to have its core."

Watch On Proof that Warframe has the juice: Werner Herzog explaining the game in the most inexplicable yet cool way possible.

But while Soulframe may be the future, there's no interest in stepping back from Warframe—in fact, Carter said skyrocketing prices driven by the rampocalypse could actually help keep Warframe relevant for years to come.

"You can play Warframe on your PS5 Pro and it looks sweet, cutting edge. And you can also play it on a four-generations-ago Android phone," Carter said. "And so for me, I hope that if console demands aren't able to be kept up with, or people need to look at older hardware because the new stuff is so expensive, they're still going to have Warframe to play, because it's a forever game that's always being updated."

items.title: Every year, fans of this post-apocalyptic shooter game flock to London, Ont. by the thousands
Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’
items.summary: Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game
items.content:
Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / Generate transcript A transcript unlocks clips, previews, and editing. 5 2 Destiny’s biggest rival Warframe has had ‘two years of massive growth’ Digital Extremes believes in console growth, and discusses the ‘careful’ development of its second game Christopher Dring Jul 28, 2026 5 2 Share Transcript Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Digital Extremes’ Sheldon Carter on…

Bungie’s ‘looter shooter’ Destiny was a real thorn in the side of Warframe.

The Digital Extremes game had launched 18 months earlier, and found itself facing off against a better resourced rival.

“There’s a lot of overlap between the two games,” says Digital Extremes president Sheldon Carter.

“Destiny 1 really hit us when it came out. It’s a looter shooter with tons of marketing and really great developers on the team. Destiny 2 as well.”

In May this year, Bungie announced the end of Destiny. It would no longer be making updates to the series. And since then, most of the Destiny team has been laid off.

“For a while we thought about [Destiny] as competition and we were aggressively wanting to compete with what they’re doing. But over time, developers from their team come onto our team. New people who we started, they learnt what looter shooters are because they’ve put thousands of hours into Destiny. And so, at our studio, it was a bit of mourning with that news. The mood was pretty dour.

“The budgets and the competition to keep putting updates out… it’s really difficult and every studio has its own culture and different way of doing things. I can’t imagine [what it’s like] with a studio as big as Bungie, which also had Marathon going on, and a lot of different things pulling them in a lot of directions. Honestly, for me, it’s more sadness that it’s over. I hope the best for all the people there.”

Sheldon Carter, Digital Extremes Warframe is in a very different position. Five years ago, Digital Extremes felt that the game had peaked and it began work on a new game, a multiplayer RPG called Soulframe.

“Some people in the company were like, ‘Oh, Warframe’s peaked. And as it gradually goes to the West, we will have to start something new.” And while we did start another project, we changed our focus about how we were developing Warframe, how we were promoting it, and we’ve had a few years of straight just massive growth.

“Now we’re in this happy position where Warframe’s really thriving, and that gives us the ability to give Soulframe a tone of rope to try stuff out.”

Keywords Studios is the games industry’s end-to-end partner, with over 13,000 people across 26 countries helping studios build, launch and grow games at global scale. Supercharged by technology and shaped by long-term partnership, Keywords Studios connects specialist expertise around the player experience.

For game development, that means flexible production support that scales with ambition. From co-development and engineering to live operations and technical delivery, Keywords Studios helps teams move faster, solve complexity and keep production connected, without losing sight of the game players are waiting for.

Although Warframe lacks the profile of Destiny, the game and its studio is still a significant operation. Digital Extremes, which is owned by Tencent, now has over 500 staff.

items.title: Amir’s Shockwave Coming Soon
items.summary: Hearing a hiccup or two in the signal, Tenno? That’s because the infamous Hex hacker is taking over Nightwave with Nightwave Mix: Amir’s Shockwave, which arrives on August 12 ! Past and future collide in this electrifying Nightwave full of
items.content:
Hearing a hiccup or two in the signal, Tenno? That’s because the infamous Hex hacker is taking over Nightwave with Nightwave Mix: Amir’s Shockwave, which arrives on August 12! Past and future collide in this electrifying Nightwave full of all-new Rewards that will undoubtedly add a (shocking) spring to your step.

Rewards Include:

This time around, you can earn the 1999-themed Globakk Syandana, Kaneshell Atomicycle Regalia, Teisatz Oculus and much, much more! Stay tuned for more details on all the rewards up for grabs as we get closer to the event. So don’t swap stations just yet, as we’ll have more information regarding Nightwave Mix: Amir’s Shockwave when it releases on August 12.

Fables & Frontiers: Running Late

Entirely separate from this new series of Nightwave Mix Rewards, there’s also the brand-new six-day KIM mini narrative adventure in the form of Fables & Frontiers: Running Late, releasing on August 12! Allow the mischievous technophile Amir to guide you through this bite-sized take on the Fables & Frontiers tabletop game from the world of Warframe: 1999. To unlock Fables & Frontiers: Running Late, you must complete The Hex Quest’s finale and reach Rank 5 with The Hex Syndicate and a KIM Chemistry of “Close” (Rank 5) with Amir himself. Earn several new Rewards from Fables & Frontiers: Running Late, including an all-new Atomicycle Key Sugatra, Fables & Frontiers Glyphs for each member of The Hex, several returning items from Nora's Mix Vol. 8 and much more! All of these can be redeemed from Amir by ringing the bell in a new area of The Höllvania Central Mall in exchange for Hex Standing. Please Note: Fables & Frontiers: Running Late is a permanent addition to the KIM System that you can access anytime by meeting the correct prerequisites and is not tied to Nightwave Mix: Amir’s Shockwave.

What is Nightwave?

Experiencing this facet of Warframe for the first time? Nightwave is a pirate radio broadcast hosted by Nora Night (or, in this case, Amir of The Hex), focused on the latest stories in the Origin System. Nightwave is also a series of Daily, Weekly and now Acts. All of which offer new and useful (and often entirely unique) Rewards! Nightwave is available via the Base of Operations’ Navigation console, through the Orbiter’s radio scanner (located on the left side of your Orbiter’s bridge), or via the Pause Menu UI. In the Nightwave menu, you’ll see your progress through the current mix, your current Reward Tiers, as well as a rotating set of Daily, Weekly, Elite Weekly and Permanent Weekly Acts. Stick with Nightwave each day and get some fantastic Customizations!

items.title: After years of failing to get into MMOs, Warframe finally won me over in 2026
items.content:
Digital Extremes' sci-fi game has finally ensnared me, and I'm now even more excited for Soulframe

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Until I played Warframe , the MMO had always been a hard sell for me. The constant updates and endless narrative expansions as seen in World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy 14 intimidate like nothing else in the video game world. I almost always crave the comfort of knowing I'm progressing towards a logical end point – at least when it comes to story-driven games – and the best MMOs , as a rule, seek to go on for eternity.

So despite my efforts, games like Black Desert Online, Fallout 76 , and Genshin Impact lose me soon after I start, simply because I can't accept the potentially limitless experiences on offer. How am I supposed to feel satisfied with my progress if there's no end destination? Well, one game recently changed my mind.

I first tried Warframe over a decade ago on Xbox One but quickly bounced off it. This was a different time in my life, before I could appreciate single-player live service games like Diablo 4 and arguably Fortnite . Even the original Destiny didn't hold my attention, so maybe it was a sci-fi thing? No, that wasn't it – what futuristic FPS could compare to Titanfall back in the day? Or now, for that matter?

But when I went to TennoCon earlier this month, I saw Digital Extremes' long-running epic in a whole new light. The game's community is held in high regard, and it was almost immediately clear as to why. The fans attending the convention were enthusiastic, friendly and generous, praising cosplays and handing out stickers in the name of Warframe and Soulframe, the latter being Digital Extremes' latest work currently in early access on PC only.

As I breathed in the atmosphere, I knew I had to try Warframe again – so I installed the free-to-play title on my Xbox Series X when I got home and jumped in. I chose my first playable biomech warframe (Volt, if you're curious), and began exploring the numerous planets, enemies and loot all crying out for my undivided attention.

Warframe head's advice for live service devs is to "make a good game before they kick you out" Guild Wars 3 may have cracked the MMO code for tired millennials In a world filled with live service games, MMORPGs are finding new ways to flourish (War)frame of Mind Unlike many of the new games I've been playing in recent years, Warframe is 100% a power fantasy. Right out of the gate, I was blasting foes to bits with firearms, cleaving through them with blades, and electrocuting them with my warframe's unique abilities.

It all felt wonderful. There was no immediate challenge like Elden Ring , or intrinsic sense of vulnerability like Resident Evil Requiem (the Grace sections, anyway). This isn't to say I don't enjoy FromSoftware and Capcom games – because I do – but the change of pace is refreshing in 2026.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

(Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) (Image credit: Digital Extremes) Image 1 of 4 View Original

As for the all-important narrative element that usually leaves me frustrated in an MMO, I was saved from my usual despair by simply not knowing what was happening. This tracked with what creative director Rebb Ford told GamesRadar+ when we interviewed her recently: "You will have no idea what's going on, and that's okay," she said with a smile, and she was right on the money. Luckily for me, the old adage of 'ignorance is bliss' rang true, because I was having too much fun dishing out damage to care who or what a Tenno was.

So why couldn't I stop worrying and learn how to love the MMO before? In truth, I don't entirely know, but the satisfyingly slick combat and traversal of Warframe certainly plays a part. Each time I begin a mission, I hurl my warframe head-first into the mayhem, shooting, slicing and ability-ing my way through the enemy hordes without a care for why I'm doing it. Yes, I have the guiding voice of Lotus, the game's matriarchal figure (and voiced by Rebb Ford), for support, but I don't pay too much mind to the why , merely the what ..

And yet, my mind wanders from time to time. I think about Lotus, Teshin, and the other NPCs I've made contact with in Digital Extremes' universe, and I want to know their histories, motivations, hopes, and everything else about them. The thing is, I'm in no rush. Warframe has enough content to keep players occupied for a long time – between 114 and 1,556 hours according to How Long to Beat – so I'll find the answers when I'm ready.

items.title: ‘Warframe’ @ TennoCon ’26: “Tau” Welcomes You to a New Star Chart
items.summary: Today, during TennoCon 2026, developer Digital Extremes celebrated 11 years of TennoCon with its record-breaking community celebration today attended by
items.content:
Mobile News Nintendo PC PlayStation Xbox Genghis Husameddin

Today, during TennoCon 2026, developer Digital Extremes celebrated 11 years of TennoCon with its record-breaking community celebration today attended by thousands of guests and streamed live to millions of fans around the world—and they rewards these nerds with a new look at the next major narrative event for their free-to-play looter shooter title ‘Warframe’: Welcome to “Tau”, the next System in Warframe’s expanding universe. The Tau System will launch this year, taking players to an all-new Star Chart. The look that was provided featured Warframe’s new noir detective Warframe, Brysko, who features an internal monologue voiced by the Matthew Mercer (‘The Legend of Vox Machina’, ‘Final Fantasy VII Rebirth’), Warframe‘s first-ever card mini-game, Portau, based on the mechanics of poker, and a fall update titled Iceblade of Narin. Additionally, the developer unveiled Citrine Prime Access, a new take on Warframe’s free battle pass, Nightwave, titled Shockwave, hosted by Protoframe Amir (Volt), and the Mesa Heirloom Collection. Check out all the details below (there is a lot, oh my goodness (music, reworks, Amir, etc etc) and know that TennoCon 2027 will be back in London, Ontario, Canada between 16-17 July 2027. Good grief we really are inching toward the 2030s…

WARFRAME: TAU (2026): Reach beyond the bounds of the Origin System in Warframe’s next major Narrative Chapter. Venture to a new Star Chart, the Tau System, and see what has become of it and the Sentient residents of Fornax and another yet-to-be-seen location…

MESA HEIRLOOM COLLECTION (AVAILABLE TODAY!): Mesa , the outcast vagabond, rides off into the sunset in style with a new Heirloom Collection of cosmetics available today with a fashionable, toggleable poncho primed for customizing.

AMIR’S SHOCKWAVE (AUGUST): Encounter a new kind of Warframe side story via a special Nightwave remix, hosted by the Protoframe Amir ( Volt ) for a collection of Warframe: 1999-themed cosmetics. Return to the K.I.M. messaging system for a new mini-role-playing adventure with The Hex crew full of magic dice, formidable foes, and exclusive rewards, including a new song from the in-game boy band On-lyne: RUNNING LATE .

ICEBLADE OF NARIN & CITRINE PRIME ACCESS (FALL 2026): Digital Extremes’ Fall update this year will be Iceblade of Narin , introducing the female ice-themed 66th Warframe, a Banshee Warframe rework and deluxe skin, as well as a deluxe skin for Qorvex. Witness the luminous luster of Citrine Prime, the crystal bastion, reliving the golden age and style of the Orokin Empire alongside new Prime weapons and accessories. Tune in to the September Devstream, hosted in Seoul, South Korea, for more details.

TENNOVIP WORLD TOUR 2026 & TENNOCON 2027: The Warframe development team is returning to their global trek across our planet to connect with players everywhere in-person this year with events planned for South Korea, China, London, and Glasgow. TennoCon will also once again make its return to London, Ontario, Canada on July 16-17, 2027 for the acclaimed community event’s 12th year. Stay tuned to Warframe’s official website, forums, and social channels for more details soon.

Soulframe also saw its panel and, with it, the announcement of its latest Fable, dubbed “Warsongs”. You can read more about it right over here!

SOULFRAME’S LATEST GAMEPLAY SHOWCASE: As a part of TennoCon’s finale presentation, Soulframe’s development team debuted a brand new gameplay demo showcasing the team’s latest progress for the upcoming fantasy action RPG adventure, showcasing a new Warsongs Fable which features a corrupted player progression path, a fishing mini-game, the long-anticipated mount system, and new performances from Ben Starr and Jennifer English ( Clair Obscur: Expedition 33).

“When we launched Warframe nearly 14 years ago, we never dreamed of what it truly could become,” said Rebecca Ford , Creative Director of Warframe . “With community at our side, our little passion project blossomed into something more, something meaningful beyond business metrics, beyond player count, beyond data and numbers. Now, we look beyond the stars at this next chapter, and we reach into our hearts with the deepest bow we could ever give to say ‘thank you’ to our community who have trusted us, respected us, and who have helped us shape this big little game into something more than we could have ever imagined. Warframe is for you, Tau is for you, and we are so excited to experience this journey with you together.”

Warframe is available across PC via Warframe.com /Steam (Windows & Linux via Proton), Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo Switch consoles, iOS, and Android devices. Full cross-save and crossplay are supported across all platforms. And again, Warframe’s Tau update will be coming this way later this year.

Head over and let us know your thoughts in the Day O ne Forums , the perfect place to chat about games if you’re a little more old-school and prefer things in a longform format.

Prefer the chaos of live and fast moving conversation? Come and make some noise in the lively DayOne Community Discord Server instead. If you’re rocking a DayOne Membership, both places give special access for our supporters, and you’ll unlock a ton of exclusive content, just for you.

items.title: Destiny 2’s Demise Is ‘Existentially Threatening,’ Says ‘Warframe’ Creative Director
items.summary: Another game in the live-service shooter genre, Warframe, has been running in parallel with Destiny for ages, maintaining perhaps greater consistency over time,
items.content:
Gaming Destiny 2’s Demise Is ‘Existentially Threatening,’ Says ‘Warframe’ Creative Director By Paul Tassi ,

Forbes contributors publish independent expert analyses and insights. News and opinion about video games, television, movies and the internet. Follow Author Jul 13, 2026, 11:11am EDT Jul 13, 2026, 04:46pm EDT --:-- / --:-- This voice experience is generated by AI. Learn more . This voice experience is generated by AI. Learn more . Warframe/Marathon Digital Extremes, Bungie Well, this would happen in any normal season of Destiny 2, but the game is starting its downward slope in terms of players departing. It is not an abrupt drop-off, which is great to see, and it’s still performing well a month after its final update, Monument of Triumph. But there’s the rub, the final update. Nothing else is coming here for the formerly live game.

Another game in the live-service shooter genre, Warframe , has been running in parallel with Destiny for ages, maintaining perhaps greater consistency over time, and still surviving, even thriving to this day. But rather than celebrate a “win” over the departed Destiny , it’s making its higher-ups sad and nervous. Some new comments come from Warframe Creative Director Rebb Ford in an interview with GamesRadar during the recent TennoCon:

"It's horrible news, because it shows that even if you care so much, the business side of this industry always gets the last remark.”

"Those are the types of stories and experiences that, when you're in a position where you have your own game, your own IP, and you work as hard as you do on it... That's not the first time it's happened, and it'll happen again, where the business aspect of the video game economy makes the decision for you, and it is existentially threatening at every level, because the idea that we aren't in charge of our own goodbye is something I wake up thinking about every single day."

Destiny 2 Bungie In the case of Destiny , there were years-long plans for the second game, and if it was up to the devs at Bungie, most would eagerly have hopped on board the production of a Destiny 3. But cost, cost, cost killed the game, partly due to poor management decisions that exacerbated those costs, and partly due to the baseline of a game that requires such an enormous investment to maintain endless live content. As I’ve previously reported, there have only been a few times in its history that Destiny 2 has been profitable.

Right until the end, you could feel the passion of the Destiny devs with an exceptional final update that put the game in its best state in years…right before there was no more new content to play. The player surge was higher than both of the last two expansions despite almost nothing new to play, and again, it maintains good numbers after a month. But those will continue falling, which cannot be helped.

Ford may be right to be nervous about the state of the industry and working on a very similar game. Warframe’s Digital Extremes does not have to answer to Sony, however, and costs are not at the same level as Destiny . But they’ve figured out a sustainable groove, and there’s no sign of the game ending any time remotely soon.

Follow me on Twitter , YouTube , and Instagram .

Pick up my sci-fi novels the Herokiller series and The Earthborn Trilogy .

items.title: Warframe: Mesa Prime Build and Review
items.summary: Mesa is a legacy warframe that has stood the test of time over the years, here is our recommended build and review for her.
items.content:
Mesa and her Prime have been in Warframe for a very long time, and at this point in the game, are still considered the most mainstream, strong, and fun frames out there. There are plenty of reasons for this. Mesa can shield herself, buff her allies, and, with the right build, mow down legions of foes with ease. Below will be our recommended build for her Prime you can try out. Followed by our review of how she’s held up over the years!

Below will be the build for her Prime, which you will need 0 formas for. Her normal version will need 2 formas:

Below will be the build for her Regulators, which you will need 1 forma for with either her normal or Prime version:

Let’s start with the main build. You will want to stack everything into power, strength, duration, and efficiency. Mesa needs her abilities to work as long as they can and to be re-castable as much as possible. Obviously, the main draw for power strength will be for her regulators, which you will need Mesa’s Waltz for mobility. Her regulators are her main damage-dealing ability. They auto target, have crazy good stats, and with Secondary Enervate , you can at least get constant orange critical hits with them.

Finally, my choices for her Archon Shards are down below. You can change these out for whatever you see fit in your playstyle.

Mesa in Warframe has really stood the test of time. To my knowledge, she is one of the only frames that has not received a full-on rework, nor does she need one. I mean, that didn’t stop Digital Extremes from reworking Nova back in the day when she was perfect as is, but still. She’s strong, crazy strong, and very durable in missions. You need Mesa’s Waltz to stay mobile and avoid death as much as possible. But with the above build, you can take any difficulty with her and shine brightly with her.

For a closer, bonus look at the Art & Animation of Warframe, click here.

AWAKEN TO A NEW SYSTEM

Warframe: Tau | Official Trailer

The path to Tau will soon open, taking you beyond the boundaries of the Origin System for the very first time. Get ready to risk it all in a brand new region of space orbiting a binary star and teeming with new experiences.

Get ready to risk it all. Warframe: Tau arrives later this year.

TennoCon 2026 Gameplay Demo

During your first foray into the lost paradise that is the Tau System, you'll sneak into the heart of a Sentient city ruined by criminality and corruption. But this is only the beginning, and marks a new journey for Warframe with much more of Tau to come, including another as-yet-to-be-revealed location launching with the full update later in 2026. Stay tuned for more details soon.

TennoLive 2026 Relay

Those who entered this year's in-game TennoLive Relay bore witness to a wild new addition to the Tenno fleet: their very own Vessel. You can still jump in and experience it for yourself until the Relay closes on July 13 at 10 a.m. ET. Think you missed out? Think again! Starting July 13, any Tenno who has completed Vor's Prize will be able to see and personalize their Vessel from ANY Dry Dock on the Star Chart. Keep watch for Arturos and Zioa, who will answer their calling later this year…

Enter a Sentient Metropolis

Your journey in this new Star Chart begins in the Bloom-soaked decay of Fornax, a lawless ring city densely populated with all manner of degenerates and drenched in unending waves of madness-inducing black rain. Between the addicts in its slums and the thugs working its docks, reaching the casino at the heart of this urban hellscape requires quick wits and an even quicker trigger finger.

Scour the Streets with Brysko

A noir-inspired Warframe working with Albrecht Entrati to infiltrate the Sentient criminal underworld, Brysko chases down leads with a relentlessness matched only by his cynicism. Although silent to the world, his inner monologue belies an honorable ethos… at least until the occasion calls for his Corecracker or Rain & Shine — an Exalted Pistol and a pair of brutal Fist weapons, respectively.

Tangle with the Fornax Drowners

The enforcers, hired hands and knucklebusters standing in your way comprise a new faction of Sentient enemies who have evolved far and away from the familiar foes of the Origin System. Though you're more than equipped to take them out, don't get too cocky, especially when the black rain begins to fall…

Defy the Hunra

Control over the many rackets in Fornax rests with the Hunra, a brutal kingpin at the center of the Sentient underbelly who enthusiastically dispenses violence, fear and Bloom to maintain his seat at the head of the table. To reach him, you'll need to overcome his legions of loyalists, any of whom would happily dispatch you to curry favor with the Boss, who seems as untouchable as he is implacable.

Try your hand at Portau

Fortune rarely smiles in Fornax, but when it does, the gamblers hunched at the casino's Portau tables earn the closest thing here to an honest living. Warframe's first original card game is built on unique suits of Blooms, Cores, Moons and Suns, and offers some welcome excitement amidst the hustle and heartbreak of Tau. Why not test your luck and play a few hands for yourself?

New Music: "View From The Top"

Doomy, gloomy, yet undeniably stylish, our Gameplay Demo's seductive allure was all the more potent thanks to the sultry sounds of a particular musical number sung by Sentient crooner Larynde. If you haven't heard it yet (or just want an immediate re-listen), the visualizer for "View From The Top" is also now available on the Official Warframe YouTube Channel.

COMING THIS FALL

Iceblade of Narin

Our Fall 2026 update has been named! Before you venture beyond the Origin System to Tau, we will first introduce the 66th Warframe, two new Deluxe Collections, a highly-anticipated Rework, the next Prime Access release and more. Join us for our next Devstream on September 4 to learn more.

Banshee Deluxe and Rework

Darkness comes for the scream queen with her first Deluxe Collection since 2016: a suite of Customizations evoking nightmares and the nocturnal, designed by community artist Mischka. Banshee mains can also look forward to an upcoming Rework that will improve her sound-based Abilities and overall playability.

Qorvex Deluxe

We're working hard to spruce up Albrecht Entrati's original designs for his indomitable, concrete-based Warframe, Qorvex. With a new Skin and Customizations inspired by gargoyles and gothic architecture, this radioactive behemoth has never looked better.

Citrine Prime Access

The luminously lustrous Citrine will receive a Prime polishing when she enters Prime Access later this year, crystalizing her greatness with pristine, golden glam. She'll release alongside upgraded Prime Weapons, Accessories and more, which we'll reveal in greater detail soon, so stay tuned.

SOULFRAME

Warsongs: A Soulframe Fable

A splinter in the heart, sings in the dream.

Meet Bayor, an Envoy like yourself but sworn to Synod and the Ode. Venture back to memories of your childhood with Doyen. Ride into the fray on wolf-back as you confront the threat in the present. Embrace the corruption of the Vadagar as a new path to progression in Soulframe.

Full Soulframe Recap

Read the complete event recap for more details on the unveiling of a new Pact, the upcoming addition of fishing, long-awaited mounts and the Mendicant Reinbreaker which awaits your challenge in-game right now. Or hear the details from the developers themselves with the TennoCon 2026 Soulframe Devstream, available here.

EVENTS

Amir's Shockwave

Get ready for a shakeup like you've never heard before! This August, Amir of the Hex will be cutting through the airwaves (and across space and time) to bring you a double-dose of 1999-themed content. Not only will he be hosting his own remixed edition of Nightwave replete with never-before-seen Rewards, but he'll also be joining his Protoframe teammates for a unique KIM narrative adventure, Fables & Frontiers: Running Late.

TennoVIP 2026 Tour

We're set to connect with more Tenno than ever thanks to a host of new TennoVIP events around the world. With Warframe developers set to visit South Korea, China, London and Glasgow, this could be your chance to meet up for the ultimate IRL experience. Ticket registration for future stops will go live at a later date, so keep an eye on our official social channels.

Dog Days 2026

What's summer without a trip to the beach? Warframe's hottest seasonal event returns on August 4 with sizzling Rewards including four new Glyphs designed by community artist SpaceWaifu.

Warframe x Fortnite

Warframe's original swordsman brings his mastery of the blade to the world of Fortnite! For the first time, Tenno can squad up, drop into the Island, and outrun the storm as the legendary Warframe with a brand-new Excalibur Outfit.

PACKS & MERCH

Mesa Heirloom Collection

Our latest hallowed Heirloom Collection is now available! The legendary gunslinger, Mesa, has new Customizations to keep your spurs jingling, including her signature brimmed Signa and travel-worn Duster attachments featuring additional toggles so you can always adjust her look to your liking. https://store.steampowered.com/app/4735410/Warframe_Mesa_Heirloom_Collection/

TennoCon 2026 Merch

Warframe's biggest day of the year may be over, but you can still keep the party going with the TennoCon 2026 Merch Pack. Show the world you were there when Warframe moved beyond the Origin System to Tau with this year's exclusive IRL Customizations.

TennoCon 2026 Giveaways

There's still time to enter our celebratory giveaways and secure your chance to win some truly stellar prizes — including gaming gear from HyperX, the Stalker jersey from Champion, Platinum from yours truly, and a powerful, customized PC from OMEN. Good luck, Tenno! Enter Now!

Community

Cosplay Contest

Our annual Cosplay Contest returned to the Canada Life Place, with a fresh roster of designs from around the Origin System. Contenders were judged on performance and craftsmanship by special guest judges, to the resounding cheers of their fellow Tenno.

Art Showcase

The Origin System’s finest artists delivered once again! Contest finalists saw their work displayed for all to behold at TennoCon — a testament to the passion and creativity of Tenno from all over the world.

Dojo Showcase

Presenting your winners of the #TennoCon 2026 Dojo Showcase! Participating decorators were invited to submit their best in-game builds from over the past two years. With more than 75 submissions from three different Warframe builds, narrowing down the winners was no easy feat.

SPECIAL THANKS

Sistema Toronto

Sistema Toronto is a free after-school music and social development program for children living in underserved communities with the end goal of transformative social action. Your donations allow Sistema Toronto students to play real instruments, receive instruction with professional musicians, eat a healthy snack every day, and benefit from a community of support.

London Cares

London Cares Homeless Response Services delivers frontline support to chronic homelessness through street outreach, supportive housing, and housing stability services. By integrating housing with health, income, and community supports, they help people achieve lasting stability while strengthening the systems that serve them

Hoku Props

Award winning propmakers Hoku Props returned to TennoCon with another iconic cosplay: Father Lyon Allard, the Harrow Protoframe! Meticulously crafted with an astounding attention to detail, this was one of their most faithful designs yet — an impressive tribute to an iconic character from last year's The Old Peace (and his many devoted fans).

arborealkey

France-based costume and prop creator arborealkey crafted a most captivating cosplay for Sister Marie Leroux, and her ethereal presence was one of the highlights of the showfloor here in London, Ontario.

Blink

Blink certainly stepped up to the challenge with their latest project: Old War veteran and infamous heartthrob, Roathe. With a loving eye and the incredible attention to detail they're known for, they brought this fearsome figure to life as faithfully as we could have fathomed.

Plexi Cosplay

Plexi Cosplay brought to life the Brewer of Hues, Verminia! Delighting Soulframe fans on the convention floor with astute aura assessments, her presence was as lively as her designs are delightful.

items.summary: This year's TennoLive mainstage presentation took us beyond the limits of the Origin System to Tau, a place that until now has only existed in our collective dreams (and of course, memories via The Old Peace). Community Director Megan Evere
items.content: This year's TennoLive mainstage presentation took us beyond the limits of the Origin System to Tau, a place that until now has only existed in our collective dreams (and of course, memories via The Old Peace). Community Director Megan Everett guided Tenno through their first foray into Warframe's first ENTIRELY NEW star system, which will include fresh worlds to explore as ongoing cinematic narrative flourishes in a massive new region beyond anything you've ever known. Coming to all platforms later this year, our next major update will begin to answer the question: "What has become of Tau?" While the future will ultimately offer a wider look at this vast binary star system, the path to get there begins in Fornax — a sprawling Sentient metropolis consisting of Slums, Docks, and seedy gambling dens. The extent of Fornax's corruption is apparent in both the addicts and criminals who populate it, as well as the unending black rain that pours down on them during frequent storms… with horrifying results. Albrecht Entrati is already here, having enlisted the help of a new, noir-inspired Warframe named Brysko to help him infiltrate the Sentient underworld and reach the Hunra. This fearsome kingpin maintains control of Fornax's many rackets through violence, intimidation and fear, and it will be up to you to reach him in time to avert the breakout of a cataclysmic new conflict. With the return of old friends, old foes and old wounds gone-but-not-forgotten, Tau will confront you with horrifying consequences from your past, and an incredibly bright new canvas for the evolving future of Warframe. Learn more by visiting our official webpage for Warframe: Tau here and be sure to watch our upcoming Devstreams at twitch.tv/warframe for more details on the journey that lies ahead.

items.title: Warframe’s Next Expansion Is the Epic Payoff to 13 Years of Storytelling
items.summary: Warframe Tau might be Digital Extremes' version of Bungie's Destiny 2 expansion The Final Shape.
items.content:
Warframe Tau might be Digital Extremes' version of Bungie's Destiny 2 expansion The Final Shape.

A new Warframe will plunge into never before seen worlds in the Warframe Tau expansion.

Over the past few years, Warframe players have spent much of their time in-game exploring a broken timestream, jumping from one era to the next in their fight against an eldritch space god .

But at its TennoCon 2026 event, developer Digital Extremes revealed a bold new direction for the game: Instead of exploring time, players will soon enter an entirely new part of outer space. The Tau solar system teased in The Old Peace update will soon be accessible during regular gameplay, with multiple new celestial bodies for players to explore.

Live-service games that thrive for years get the rare chance to morph and evolve into something new. When Warframe launched in 2013, it was a simple third-person looter-shooter about deadly robotic ninjas. Now it features raid bosses, an endless roguelike mode, a semi-open-world fishing simulator and even some visual novel elements .

In an industry that seems increasingly reluctant to take risks on new ideas, Digital Extremes continues to reinvent its sci-fi brainchild. Each new update includes creative leaps leading to “out-there” ideas like a living guitar or a spider-themed robot , ensuring there’s no other game quite like Warframe.

Even so, all those zany ideas existed within a single solar system — disparate story threads connected by a common location. The boundaries of the world have always been well-defined by the in-game star chart. In the next expansion, that’s changing for the first time ever.

Leaving behind the Origin System will introduce players to worlds that are more alien than they’ve ever seen before.

Warframe players have been hacking, slashing and bullet-jumping across the Origin System — a starchart that mirrors our real-world solar system with some sci-fi alterations — for over 13 years. Soon it’ll be time to explore a new frontier: Tau.

It’s difficult to express how massive this change feels without pointing toward the other sci-fi looter-shooter cultural juggernaut, Bungie’s Destiny and Destiny 2.

The Destiny series — first released in 2014, just one year after Warframe — also took place largely within the boundaries of our very own solar system. For years, players battled the forces of darkness across the surface of Earth, Mars and other familiar planets.

But when Destiny 2’s decade-long narrative reached its climax in The Final Shape expansion , players plunged into the heart of the living planet-like Traveler in order to battle the villainous Witness. When the stakes were highest, players were transported to a completely alien locale within the deity-like sphere they’d followed for Destiny’s entire plot, a place where everyone was on equal footing and many long-standing questions were finally answered.

Warframe Tau looks like it’ll provide answers to some longstanding questions — like what deal the Lotus struck with the eldritch Man in the Wall.

While Warframe’s narrative has flirted with the idea of sending players to Tau for years now, the reality of finally heading to a brand new star chart feels monumental.

items.title: As Video Game Industry Burns, Warframe's Devs Aren't Taking Anything For Granted
items.summary: “I feel very lucky to be working on this game and to have this dev team and the community that we’ve built, because I’m no stranger to the fact that it could all end tomorrow"
items.content:
After over a decade of building to this moment, Warframe is finally headed to Tau, the solar system where its vast, endearingly strange narrative began. Tau isn’t just a quest or an area to roam; it is, like the Origin System that comprises much of Warframe to date, a series of planets that players will do missions across. Today at TennoCon in London, Ontario, Digital Extremes debuted the first region of that interconnected pocket of space, Fornax. It’s a truly momentous occasion—perhaps the game’s most ambitious addition yet.

But at the end of a TennoCon preview event earlier this week, creative director Rebb Ford let some relatable hesitation show through: "It's obviously a huge, scary time for us,” she said, “because the games industry is super stable right now, and it's awesome to show something that may or may not impact the future of the company."

Warframe , which began as a humble co-op space ninja shooter and evolved into a sprawling sci-fi epic with too many gameplay systems to count and one of the most dedicated communities in video games , has proven remarkably resilient in an era where live-service games drop like flies. Even Destiny 2 —to which Warframe is often (if erroneously) compared—met what basically amounted to its untimely end earlier this year.

And of course, Microsoft’s latest round of layoffs remains all too fresh on everyone’s minds as hardware prices skyrocket and Sony adapts by killing physical discs . Change is afoot, with traditional triple-A games looking more and more like a potential casualty. No one is safe and nothing is sacred. Not even a seemingly unshakable pillar like Warframe .

“It’s fucking awful, what’s happening in this industry,” community director Megan Everett told Aftermath during a recent interview. “I feel very lucky to be working on this game and to have this dev team and the community that we’ve built, because I’m no stranger to the fact that it could all end tomorrow. Games as a service, it's a scary world. We've been doing it for 13 years, and we have no secret formula. We have no cheat code. We have just stayed in our little Canadian homebrew lane, put our heads down, and really tried to make this game what we want and what our community wants it to be.”

For developers at Digital Extremes, that has at various points meant eschewing trends and sticking to their many, many guns.

"I think back to when PUBG and Fortnite were popping off,” said Everett, “and everyone was making a battle royale game, and I remember internally we all looked at each other like 'We're not doing that.’"

"That's not what our expertise is, and we know where our strengths are,” Everett continued. “We know where we can stray a little bit and get wacky and weird, and so we do that. But it would be a disservice if we went so crazy that [we lost sight of Warframe 's identity]. Like, we've tried the PvP thing; we've tried Conclave. It didn't work, and we know that's not what we're about, so we shifted to focusing on the story and the narrative. I think that has been a good thing for us in that we know where our strengths are."

The TennoCon Tau demo leaned into those narrative proclivities, with cinematic flourishes aplenty. An intro to the new solar system that—if you’re a longtime Warframe player—was frankly chill-inducing gave way to a perspective switch to an all-new Warfame, Brysko, a creation of Albrecht Entrati, the Void-harnessing scientist who set much of Warframe ’s story into motion. Brysko’s whole thing is that he’s basically an old-timey noir detective in Warframe form. Lacking a mouth to call his own, he monologues about everything that happens to him in his head—which, of course, the player can hear, even though no one else can.

But why a noir detective to introduce a new solar system? Because there are mysteries afoot in both the cosmic and more immediate senses. And also because Ford really liked Law And Order as a kid (Brysko = Briscoe, by the way) and Blade Runner as an adult.

"I wanted [those inspirations] in Warframe ,” said Ford. “It's kind of that juvenile, but I wanted Warframe to explore gangs, addiction, [and] lifespan of constructs. All of these things are super relevant to Sentients, who as a construct were created by man—no different than androids. So this was essential for the tone of Tau's first reveal."

The idea of a monologuing Warframe followed shortly after.

"Credit to Adrian, our lead writer, because we were trying to think of how to go noir and tell the world of Tau from a perspective that needs to feel new, and he really put his heart out on his sleeve and was like 'I really think we could get an inner monologue working for this,”' said Ford. “We proved it within a day. We were like 'That's it, that has to be it.' Because nothing else would work in the world with the pieces we put on the chessboard. It's too bleak, it's too dark, it's too weird, and the unknowable inner monologue of this character felt very extreme, but in my heart and soul, I feel like it works. And if it works for at least just me, then you know what? Happy early Christmas to me."

What ensued in the TennoCon demo was a stroll through a grimy, goopy noir slum—if H.R. Giger was in the business of imagining such places. Sentients, addicted to a drug called Bloom, writhed and in some cases attacked as Brysko waxed nihilistic about their dead-end lives in the universe’s rock bottom. “All dreaming or dead,” he said of the Sentients at one point. “Until the rains come.” But in his cheery estimation, things could always be worse: “At least I’m not out on one of the old battlefields,” he growled mid-combat, voiced by the inimitable Matt Mercer, who made the hammy dialogue a lot more convincing. “Warframes and Sentients lurching back to life, fighting old wars over and over again. Mindless. Heartless. Dead.”
